title: fix(core): type `resolveRecordSourceConfig`'s `data` by the arm it is already told
body:
Fixes #9473

`resolveRecordSourceConfig` in `@object-ui/core` takes a REQUIRED `dataArm` argument precisely because blocks declare `data` differently per block — its own docblock says there is no repo-wide default, *"because the answer differs per block and a default is how the second de-facto contract got in"*. Its parameter nevertheless declared a flat `data?: ViewData`, a discriminated union over four strict OBJECT arms with no array member, while its rung-1 predicate `authoredDataIsOnTheDeclaredArm` takes `unknown` and admits an ARRAY on the `'array'` arm. The declaration contradicted the contract the same function documents and implements.

## The corpus — every caller, what it passes on `data`, and which arm it declares

Read on `origin/main` `aced50d2e`, 2026-09-18T21:12Z. Five production call sites, all passing a literal arm:

| caller | schema type it passes | that type's `data` member | arm | the flat `ViewData` declaration was |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ObjectGrid.tsx` `getDataConfig` | `ObjectGridSchema` | `ViewData` (optional) | `'view-data'` | **right** |
| `ObjectMap.tsx` `getDataConfig` | `ObjectMapSchema` | `ViewData` (optional) | `'view-data'` | **right** |
| `ObjectGantt.tsx` `rawDataConfig` | `ObjectGanttSchema` | `ViewData` (optional) | `'view-data'` | **right** |
| `ObjectTree.tsx` `dataConfig` | `ObjectTreeSchema` | no `data` member declared at all | `'undeclared'` | vacuous — nothing is passed on the key |
| `ObjectCalendar.tsx` `dataConfig` | a three-member projection of `ObjectCalendarSchema`, whose `data` is `SpecObjectCalendarProps['data']` = `unknown[]` (optional) | `unknown[]` (optional) | `'array'` | **wrong**, and held shut by a cast |

So the card's claim re-derives, and its real shape is the last column: the declaration was right for three callers, vacuous for one, and wrong for exactly one — the block the arm parameter exists for. On `main` the wrong one compiled only because `ObjectCalendar.tsx` wrote `data: schema.data as ViewData | undefined`, in a comment that reported the defect as an upstream one rather than claiming it was fine.

**Measured, same tree, same command** — remove that cast on unmodified `aced50d2e` and `packages/plugin-calendar`'s `type-check` exits **2**:

```
src/ObjectCalendar.tsx(443,7): error TS2322: Type 'unknown[] | undefined' is not assignable to type
  '{ provider: "object"; object: string; } | { provider: "api"; ... } | ... '
```

⚠️ **One thing in the card is out of date and is corrected here**: the card quotes a **TS2345** at `ObjectCalendar.tsx(386,62)`, measured when the whole node was handed to the ladder. objectui#8651 changed that call to pass the three members one by one, so today the same contradiction surfaces as a **TS2322** on the object literal's `data` member. Same defect, different diagnostic — the card's error text no longer reproduces verbatim.

## What changed

The `data` member is now `AuthoredRecordSourceData` — a new exported conditional type keyed on the arm:

- `'view-data'` resolves to `ViewData`. **Unchanged**, which is why nothing moves for grid, map or gantt.
- `'array'` resolves to `unknown[]`, the shape `ComponentPropsMap['object-calendar'].data` declares (`z.array(z.unknown()).optional()`).
- `'undeclared'` resolves to `unknown`, since no published face declares a `data` row for such a block and rung 1 keeps its pre-8348 verbatim behaviour there.

⛔ **Not a union of the arms.** `ViewData | unknown[]` would let a `'view-data'` site declare a bare array and an `'array'` site declare a provider block — each of them the shape that block's row REFUSES — which is the repo-wide default `RecordSourceDataArm`'s own docblock refuses by name (AGENTS.md #0.1).

⛔ **Not overloads.** A caller holding the arm as a `RecordSourceDataArm` VARIABLE rather than a literal matches none of three literal-armed overloads; the conditional type distributes to `unknown` for it instead, so such a caller keeps compiling. That property is pinned, not assumed.

`ObjectCalendar.tsx` drops the cast (`data: schema.data`) and its now-unused `ViewData` import. The three members are still passed one by one — that spelling is what the ladder documents itself as reading.

**The card's second half**, as triage directed: two docblock passages — one in `record-source.ts`, one in `record-source-config.behaviourNeutrality-7632.test.ts` — explained `ObjectCalendar`'s retired `'data' in schema` guard by the props union `ObjectGridSchema | CalendarSchema`. objectui#8651 retired that union (`ObjectCalendarComponentProps.schema` is the published `ObjectCalendarSchema` today), so both sentences explained a guard by a type no reader can open. Both now say that clause is history at `1ec291c0` rather than a reading anyone can re-derive from `main`.

## No accept set moved

The ladder's BODY is untouched: `authoredDataIsOnTheDeclaredArm` still takes `unknown` and still decides rung 1 on the value's KIND, so every runtime verdict — including every off-arm fall-through to `staticData` then `objectName` — is what it was. Six runtime legs in the new pin file assert exactly that, through `as any` so they measure the ladder rather than the declaration. Both packages' emitted JavaScript is unchanged by this card: the only removed expression is a type assertion, which erases.

⚠️ **One compile-time refusal IS new, and it is deliberate**: a caller declaring a `ViewData` provider block under `data` while passing `'array'` no longer type-checks. That document was already refused at runtime by objectui#8348, and by `os validate` and the save gate before it — only the signature still accepted it. No caller in this repository writes it.

## Ablation — the disagreement input, both directions

Every leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from `../objectstack`: the anchor must hit exactly once, the write is verified against the disk by blob hash, and the restore is proven by `blob == HEAD` plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, with a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM against an absolute path.

**Leg A — revert the member to the flat `data?: ViewData`** (blob `1ef24ff894b1` to `1d2d6786e331`), at `4645a9864`, 2026-09-18T21:29Z. `packages/core` `type-check` goes **red, exit 2**, three errors:

```
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(88,26):  error TS2322  (arrayOnTheArrayArm — direction 1)
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(111,3):  error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(126,26): error TS2322  (arrayOnTheUndeclaredArm)
```

⛔ **Same-command control**: `providerBlockOnTheViewDataArm` did NOT error under that mutation. The ablation is arm-specific, not a blanket break.

**Leg A2 — the same mutation, this time rebuilt into `dist` before measuring the real caller**, 2026-09-18T21:30Z. Leg A's first attempt read `packages/plugin-calendar` as **green** — a false green: that program resolves `@object-ui/core` through the built `.d.ts`, which still held the fixed declaration. With `dist/utils/record-source.d.ts` reprinted as `data?: ViewData` and shown in the run's own output, `packages/plugin-calendar` `type-check` goes **red, exit 2**, at `src/ObjectCalendar.tsx(445,7)` TS2322 — the defect back at the caller the cast used to hide it at. `dist` was rebuilt from the restored source afterwards and the declaration re-read to confirm.

**Leg B — widen the type to `unknown` on every arm** (blob `1ef24ff894b1` to `24c53b50363c`), 2026-09-18T21:34Z. `packages/core` `type-check` goes **red, exit 2**:

```
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(58,3):  error TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy the constraint 'true'.
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(61,3):  error TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy the constraint 'true'.
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(104,3): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts(111,3): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
```

That is the leg that keeps this from being a mere widening: a parameter loosened to accept everything turns both directives into errors. ⛔ **Same-command control**: `_UndeclaredArmIsUnknown` and `_UndecidedArmIsUnknown` did NOT fire under it — those two arms really do resolve to `unknown` in both trees.

⚠️ The compile-time half of the pin file is **erased at runtime**; `vitest` proves nothing about it. `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` is the only program that reads it, and it was proven to read it: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists `record-source-data-arm-type-9473.test.ts` beside its sibling `record-source-config.behaviourNeutrality-7632.test.ts`, 739 files in the program.

## Acceptance notes

Verification run at `4645a9864`. Each locked run quotes the verdict line the lock printed.

- `type-check` **green** on all seven packages that touch the ladder: `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/react`, and `plugin-calendar` / `plugin-grid` / `plugin-map` / `plugin-gantt` / `plugin-tree`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/utils/ packages/types/src/__tests__/object-calendar-record-source-7313.test.ts` — **80 files, 1603 tests passed**. The last of those is the pin that reads `record-source.ts` and `ObjectCalendar.tsx` as TEXT; it stays green because the ladder's rung order, its `authoredDataIsOnTheDeclaredArm(schema.data, dataArm)` call and the calendar call's `(schema, arm)` arity are all unchanged.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/` — **37 files, 277 tests passed**.
- The new pin file's six runtime legs were re-run by name with `--reporter=verbose`, so the rows are printed rather than counted.
- Gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major` — all exit 0. `check:changeset-claims` is report-only and named no claim of mine.
- `check:doc-examples` and `check:readme-exports` **NOT MEASURED** — both print PRECONDITION-NOT-MET for unbuilt packages (*"is not on disk — run the build first"*); every one of readme-exports' 360 findings is that sentence, and its own collapsed-scan floors fire. Neither names a file in this diff. They need a whole-repo build, which is CI's run.
- Lint: a **declared narrowing**. `eslint` was run on exactly the four changed source files — exit 0, 0 errors, 4 files (count read from `--format json`). The narrowing is sound because type-aware linting is not enabled in this repo's `eslint.config.js` (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions`, no `project:` — grep exit 1, with a control grep that does find `rules:`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The seven warnings on new lines are all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` from the deliberate `as any` in the runtime control legs, the same pattern the sibling behaviourNeutrality file already carries. The repo-wide `turbo run lint` is CI's run.
- Governed surface: `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all five changed paths prints **NOT GOVERNED** (5 paths against 5 surfaces, none matched), exit 0.
- Out of scope, noted and NOT filed: `packages/plugin-map`'s test program cannot resolve `@object-ui/plugin-list` unless that package is built first, so `type-check` there is build-order sensitive in a way its siblings are not. Not a defect in this card's sense and nothing in this diff touches it; the seat that next builds a partial closure for `plugin-map` is who meets it.
